record_title: Quantitative density one for distinct consecutive products
scientific_context: Quantifies Chojecki's canonical density-one construction for distinct consecutive-block products by combining the witness-forest argument with Li's 1/24 almost-all short-prime-interval theorem.
limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The 5/6 exponent controls the short rejected-gap contribution and is not claimed optimal. The full complement is proved smaller than X/(log X)^B for every fixed B but no global polynomial power saving is obtained because the long-gap input has only a fixed-log-power exceptional-set estimate. The result concerns Chojecki's canonical greedy set and inherits the cited integral-point and prime-interval theorems. Recent concurrent work may not yet be indexed. No independent validation or formal proof-assistant verification is asserted.
